title: Leaves My Skin Soft, Hydrated, and Smelling Lovely
review: I've been using this shower oil for a while now, and it's one of the best body washes I've tried for dry skin. It cleanses gently without leaving my skin feeling tight or stripped after showering. What stands out the most is how hydrating it is. My skin feels soft and comfortable afterwards, and I don't get that dry feeling that some shower gels can leave behind. It's especially nice during colder months when my skin needs extra moisture. The scent is another thing I really enjoy. It's clean, fresh, and pleasant without being overpowering, making the whole shower feel a bit more luxurious. The large 1L bottle also lasts a long time, making it excellent value for everyday use. This is a fantastic shower oil for anyone with dry or sensitive skin who wants gentle cleansing, plenty of hydration, and a lovely fragrance.

title: Contains known skin irritants. Sulfates.
review: I’m an old school Aveda grad and skincare enthusiast. This product is marketed as “soap free” but it contains sulfates. If you have sensitive skin this product will eventually destroy your skin barrier and disrupt your microbiome. I tried to save money but ended up losing money. Sulfates are well known to produce skin irritation in a large percentage of the population. They are chemical degreasers. So while I find that my skin didn’t get dry and irritated the few times I use it, I would not use this daily on my skin. It simply well known to strip the skin of its natural oils and from there disrupt the Microbiome and with consistent use that’s exactly what would happen. I honestly didn’t think to check for sulfates because I just assumed a cleansing oil would not have that harsh ingredient. Even suave has products that have removed this ingredient. This is marketed for sensitive skin yet it contains ingredients known to cause problems with sensitive skin. It defeats the purpose of the product. I will stick with Bioderma despite it being more expensive.

title: Great Alternative to Expensive Oil Cleansers
review: I have oily combination skin and usually use DHC Deep Cleansing Oil as the first step in my double cleansing routine. After losing my DHC oil on holiday in a rural part of France, I found the Uriage Cleansing Oil in a local pharmacy. This is a slightly thicker oil and lathers when applied, but I found it to be a great first step in my routine and have now replaced it and re-purchased the larger bottle - it is great for sensitive skin, seems to balance my oily t-zone, and doesn’t break me out. Also great value for money - so much cheaper than expensive brands! Only downside is it isn’t great for removing eye make up as it can slightly sting, so would recommend a stand-alone eye make up remover if using this as part of a double cleanse skincare routine.

review: I was expecting to see changes that did not occur. It servers as a nice shower gel but it won't bring moisturizing results or change the appearance of your skin with continued use (I've been using for around 3 weeks)

title: Delicato e ne basta poco
review: L'avevo preso come detergente oleoso per il viso ma poi ho continuato anche con il corpo. Fa una leggera schiuma con una minima quantità e lascia la pelle morbida e idratata. Yuka lo valuta sufficiente mentre INCIbeauty mette più in evidenza gli ingredienti più a rischio e suggerisce prodotti alternativi migliori (vedi gli screenshot). Infatti l'avevo preso solo perché era in offerta e una buona scorta ma anche così secondo me è troppo, proverò qualcos'altro la prossima volta.
